suggestion: Capture completed-game results (final scores) from NFL.com weekly pages into `data/nfl-lab/results.json` on a schedule.
why: Without results, gates G4–G7 can never run and the leaderboard stays empty. This is the single blocking dependency.
measure: ≥200 settled NFL games archived; gate G4 turns PASS.
effort: Low — the weekly page already renders finals (e.g. Commanders 24, Giants 21).

suggestion: Archive a daily injury-report snapshot per club with the capture timestamp, instead of only the current week.
why: The official page mutates daily; a signal is only usable if we can prove the value existed before kickoff (gate G2).
owner_action: Approve snapshot storage growth (~0.2 MB/week compressed).

suggestion: Decide the market-line question explicitly: closing lines are not published by the NFL, so either license a data feed or accept that G6 can never pass.
why: Every profitability claim depends on a closing-line benchmark. This is a missing-information decision, not a coding task.
measure: G6 PASS or a written decision to drop profitability claims.
effort: Decision, then either integration or scope cut.

suggestion: Publish the depth-chart gap list as a first-class table (slots with no documented backup), refreshed weekly for all 32 clubs.
why: It is the only defensible way to answer 'is a 2nd/3rd/4th-string player replacing a starter?' from official data; today only the 49ers chart is captured.
measure: 32 club charts captured; gap count per club per week.
effort: Medium — 32 fetches, one parser per chart layout family.

suggestion: Add a 'why is this blank?' tooltip beside every UNVERIFIED cell, carrying the exact source URL that shows the gap.
why: Blank cells currently look like site errors; a reviewer needs to see the evidence for the blank in one click.
measure: 100% of blank cells carry a source link.

suggestion: Show the snapshot age in hours on every page and turn the banner amber past 48 hours.
why: Stale data is the largest silent risk in the existing dashboard: sources were 11 days old at rebuild.
measure: Age label present on 100% of pages.
status: IMPLEMENTED (this section) — the 15 legacy pages are owned by the main build and are unchanged.

suggestion: Split the 4.9 MB MLB page and 2.3 MB review page into paginated chunks or JSON-backed tables.
why: Large single pages are slow on mobile radio-network connections and hard to review line by line.
owner_action: Approve; requires editing the main build (not this session's scope).
status: DEFERRED (file owned by another build path)

suggestion: Fix the workflow triggers: `fetch-official.yml` only fires for the superseded branch name `arena/72e6d3f7-korea4` and has no schedule.
why: That is why the snapshot is stale. Main-branch pushes never refresh official sources.
measure: A refresh run on `main` plus a weekly `cron`.
owner_action: Approve workflow edit (workflow files are shared).

suggestion: Add a decision log page where each accepted suggestion is recorded with the evidence that justified it and a review date.
why: Prevents re-litigating decisions and makes reversal cheap.
measure: Every accepted item has an entry with date and review trigger.

suggestion: Retire or annotate `data/nfl-2026.json`, which still asserts `"verified": true` while citing non-official sites.
why: A file that calls itself verified but is not is worse than a missing file; it can seed future errors.
measure: File deleted or its `verified` flag set to false with a note.
owner_action: Approve deletion (it is referenced only by the audit page).
status: PROPOSED — needs approval to delete data

suggestion: Add a data-freshness SLA table per source family (schedule, injury, depth, stats) with the expected refresh cadence.
why: Turns 'is this current?' into a measured question instead of a vibe.
measure: Every source row has cadence and last-refresh columns.

suggestion: Publish the gate code, not just the gate results, and version the gate rule set.
why: Gates are the only thing separating this leaderboard from a tip sheet; they must be auditable and immutable per season.
measure: Gate rules carry version ids; changes are dated.
